about: Hand-curated map from SPEC.md §28 rows and §30 milestones to the engine tests that prove them. Consumed by deploy/evidence-report.mjs, which runs engine/test/*.test.ts and writes docs/engineering/EVIDENCE.md + evidence.json. `title` is a substring of the exact test(...) title in `file`; it must match exactly one test in that file or the report fails. Keep `approximate` honest: say what the tests do NOT show. Rows = SPEC §28; capabilities = engine capabilities beyond §28 (same shape); milestones = §30. A row with no test keeps `tests: []` and says so in `untested`.

rows.name: Wall avoidance
rows.required: A human given a destination on the other side of a wall chooses a route around it before contact; no penetration or prolonged wall sliding.

tests.title: wall: plans around the wall before contact
goal inside a wall is rejected with the blocking object named
walk around wall: completes, no penetration, no teleport, little heading jitter

rows.approximate: No explicit wall-contact-duration metric: 'no sliding' is inferred from the clearance invariant (zero violations), path length and a heading-flip bound on one synthetic wall.

rows.name: U-shaped trap
rows.required: Global planning escapes the shape; local steering alone does not oscillate indefinitely.

tests.title: U-shaped trap: global route exits via the open side
U-trap: a walker starting at the inner back wall

rows.approximate: One synthetic U and one start/goal pair; oscillation is bounded by heading flips (≤ 6) and clearance is sampled per tick from the 0.1 m clearance grid (EDT), not continuously.

rows.name: Narrow passage / two agents
rows.required: Agents pass if clearance allows; otherwise one yields/waits without jitter or repeated path flipping.

tests.title: narrow passage: uses the 1.0 m gap rather than a long detour
too-narrow passage for a wide profile is rejected / detoured, never squeezed
narrow passage: opposing walkers take turns, no overlap, no oscillation
standing person on the route: brief pause at most
runner: proving-ground walkers
C3: a walker crossing a carry waits for the load to pass
2.0 m corridor: two walkers head-on pass side by side without yielding
1.0 m gap (same scene): opposing walkers still take turns
2.0 m corridor: both walkers keep moving while passing

rows.approximate: Yielding is heuristic (traffic resources, right-of-way, passing offset), not ORCA, and not proven deadlock-free.

rows.name: Stair approach
rows.required: Agent approaches an entry region, orients appropriately, ascends valid completed steps, exits at the landing; does not climb from the side.

tests.title: stairs: oblique approach goes to the entry, faces up-stair, exits at landing
stairs: oblique start climbs real steps to the deck and ends on level 1
cancel mid-climb (review M2)

rows.approximate: Root-motion only: no foot IK, so rendered feet sink/hover by about 0.09 m on treads. Climb is a link traversal with an align phase; one straight flight on the proving ground, no landings or turns.

rows.name: Multiple floors
rows.required: Agent remains on the correct level and uses actual vertical connections instead of selecting the closest X/Y point on another floor.

tests.title: multi-level: deck → ground directly below uses stairs, never drops through
stairs: oblique start climbs real steps to the deck and ends on level 1
replan around people on the deck (review M3)

rows.approximate: Two levels (ground + one deck) on the proving ground plus progressive decks. The 2026 campus has only ground level 0 walkable (interiors and upper floors are blocked by design).

rows.name: Long load around corner
rows.required: Crew + load trajectory remains collision-free through the full maneuver; reject if rotation/clearance is impossible.

tests.title: carry: 2 people carry a 12 ft beam around the L corner of the 2.5 m corridor
carry: 19 ft upright with 4 people cannot use the 1.5 m corridor
carry: 19 ft upright goes straight down the 2.5 m corridor but cannot turn its corner
carry invariant: detects grip drift, a load inside a wall, and a wrong holder
C1: a mid-carry replan never flips the formation

rows.approximate: Rigid formation, load held level, no re-grip. Crews carry on one level only; only a single carrier may take a load up a flight (see capability 'Loads on stairs'). Collision is exact OBB vs prisms every tick; carriers have no carry/lift poses in the renderer.

rows.name: Raise tall frame
rows.required: Required crew supports the component through the raising arc; frame cannot be released before support predicate passes.

tests.title: supported bay: raise, hold, premature release refused, beams, stable release
raising arc blocked by an overhead obstacle is rejected and names it
crew too small for a 19 ft upright
raise choreography (2 people)
raise choreography (4 people)
raise choreography: an obstacle on the lifter
raise choreography (1 person, 8 ft frame)
19 ft bay: 3 people raise each 19 ft frame
C2: people holding up a frame cannot be assigned to carry

rows.approximate: The arc is sampled, not continuous; the support predicate is a rule (connections + holders), not rigid-body dynamics. The 19 ft raise is proven on open ground only (no 19 ft raise beside other structures).

rows.name: Construction changes navigation
rows.required: Installing a wall invalidates affected routes; installing usable stairs/floor can create valid new routes.

tests.title: construction changes navigation: a new wall in the gap forces a detour
construction mid-walk: new obstacle on the route triggers one replan
construction changes navigation: a stair flight set down across a walker
progressive floor: after 1 of 2 sheets only the installed sheet is walkable
full sequence: uprights → beams → release → joists → plywood → stairs → a person walks up
replan budget: construction replans are staggered deterministically

rows.approximate: Each construction epoch patches the affected grid region (bit-identical to a rebuild; no navmesh); proven on the proving ground and the progressive fixture, not on the full campus.

rows.name: Incomplete floor/stairs
rows.required: No invisible traversable surface appears simply because the final building definition contains one.

tests.title: incomplete stairs are not traversable and the failure names them
progressive floor: after 1 of 2 sheets only the installed sheet is walkable
progressive stairs: incomplete flight is not traversable and names what is missing
a sheet whose support goes missing stops being floor and is flagged

rows.approximate: Holds for engine-built decks/stairs only. The 2026 campus has no decks or stairs at all (upper floors are blocked, not modelled), so the rule is untested against historical geometry.

rows.name: Reservation conflict
rows.required: One actor/object/seat/work position cannot be simultaneously owned by incompatible actions.

tests.title: action lifecycle, reservations and diagnostics
carry: a second carry using a busy person fails with reservation.conflict
C2: people holding up a frame cannot be assigned to carry
H1: an unreachable hold station is refused at plan time
sit: two people cannot hold one camp-chair

rows.approximate: Reservations are per actor/object/slot. There are no space-time reservations: simultaneous carries are not co-planned, so sequences must order them with `after` dependencies.

rows.name: Graceful cancellation
rows.required: Cancelling a carry/raise does not cause unsupported floating/dropping unless explicitly modeled.

tests.title: carry: cancel mid-move performs a controlled set-down where the ground is clear
carry: cancel over an obstruction is refused (carry.cancel-unsafe)
carry: cancel during gather releases the crew immediately
cancel mid-raise is refused (would leave the frame unsupported)
cancel mid-climb (review M2)
H1: an unreachable hold station is refused at plan time
runner: timeout settles deferred cancels

rows.approximate: Covered for carry, raise and stairs (plus generic lifecycle cleanup). Mid-raise cancel is refused rather than modelled as a lower-back-down; install lifts (joist/plywood/beam) have no cancel test.

rows.name: Camera collision
rows.required: Cinematic camera does not pass through opaque architecture during a normal shot.

tests.title: camera collision: path keyed through the test wall is corrected
camera collision: impossible clearance is reported as rejection
camera glass: subject behind plexiglass stays readable
camera collision: a wall too tall to clear forces a deliberate, explained cut
camera geom: slab test hits walls in OBB frame and respects y range
camera geom: signed distance, placement validity, pushout

rows.approximate: The camera collides with obstacle prisms (OBBs fitted to geometry), not the render mesh; checked on 10 Hz samples plus swept segments, on the proving ground with synthetic subjects.

rows.name: Camera readability
rows.required: Important action remains visible/readable or the camera deliberately replans/cuts; no rapid oscillation.

tests.title: camera readability: subject walking behind U walls is reported
camera temporal: hysteresis prevents oscillation between two equal alternatives
camera readability: occlusion fraction, frustum, size, named reasons
camera temporal: detects A→B→A oscillation and cut density

rows.approximate: Occlusion is ray-tested against obstacle prisms, not the render mesh (no GPU/pixel visibility check); subjects are synthetic walkers, and no camera track has been rendered to video and reviewed.

rows.name: Replay independence
rows.required: Changing camera track does not alter actor routes, action results, inventory, or final world state.

tests.title: replay camera independence: camera tracks never change the take
camera replay independence: live camera solving and different planned tracks never change the take
planShotList: contiguous windows
api: take replay is independent of camera track attachment

rows.approximate: Proven at the engine/API level (take hash and final state unchanged). The browser renderer's camera path is not part of this suite.

rows.name: Fork isolation
rows.required: Edits in a workspace branch do not mutate canonical historical state or sibling branches.

tests.title: fork isolation: canonical protected; sibling branches independent
fork isolation: canonical refuses execution
rehearsal is private: history, heads and checkpoints untouched
canonical mars-2026 is protected; flagship work happens in a fork
fork isolation (room): a fork executes without touching canonical or a sibling fork

rows.approximate: Forks start from quiescent checkpoints, or mid-action only for the walking/social subset (capability 'Mid-action resumability'); there is no branch merge. The room path (EngineRoom over SQLite, the Durable Object's code) is covered here; deploy/simulation-integration.mjs repeats it over real MCP against `wrangler dev` (or SIM_BASE), which this report does not run.

rows.name: Plan invalidation
rows.required: Changing a relevant obstacle after rehearsal causes validation failure/replan before official execution.

tests.title: plan invalidation: moving an obstacle into the route after rehearsal makes execution stale
plan invalidation: env/weather, labels and provenance edits do NOT stale a plan
plan invalidation: inventory mode, RNG state and rules version are physical assumptions
tampered plans and mismatched service scenes fail loudly
api: stale plans and protected canonical workspaces are refused
plan invalidation (room): another run moving a walker onto the route stales a rehearsed plan

rows.approximate: Staleness is conservative: any physical diff (physicalHash) stales the plan, relevant to the route or not. The replan is a manual rebind by the director, not automatic. There is no design-edit engine op, so through the room the obstacle (walker s1 stepping into the 1 m passage) is moved by a second executed plan, not by editing a design entity; deploy/simulation-integration.mjs repeats this over real MCP, not run by this report.

rows.name: Replay isolation
rows.required: Viewing an old take cannot mutate a live simulation room.

tests.title: replay isolation: sampling an old take never touches history, the live workspace or the take
tampered takes are rejected
replay isolation (room): take fetches and camera tracks never change heads

rows.approximate: Engine level plus the room code (EngineRoom over node:sqlite: take fetches write zero bytes; heads, log lengths and every pose unchanged after fetches and a camera track; two rooms share nothing). The Durable Object/HTTP path — view capability refused MCP and commands, REST take fetches at several t, cross-room 404s — is proven by deploy/simulation-integration.mjs against `wrangler dev`/SIM_BASE, which this report does not run. A camera track needs the control capability (MCP) and is stored beside the take.

capabilities.name: Loads on stairs (single carrier)
capabilities.required: One person carries a component up or down a completed stair flight between levels: tilted load with step-profile clearance, exclusive flight, refusals that name the stair or missing treads.

tests.title: one person carries a stair tread from the ground up stairs A
an 8 ft 2x4 goes up too (tilted along the flight)
a 4x6 plywood panel on the 1.0 m stairs is refused
carry-stairs invariant: a load pushed into the steps mid-climb is reported
carry-stairs: determinism
someone on the flight or at its top makes the carrier wait
a walker heading up behind the carrier waits at the foot

capabilities.approximate: Single carrier only: no crews on a flight, no ladders, no turning flights or more than one flight per carry, no loads whose carry pose has a pitch (plywood on edge), no mid-flight replanning, and cancel on the flight is refused rather than modelled. One straight flight on the proving ground; the set-down check is distance only (CARRY.md 'Between levels').

capabilities.name: Social vocabulary + slots (reservation semantics)
capabilities.required: sit/stand/take_slot/face/converse/gather/campfire_circle/ambient_wander over claimable slots: one person per slot, refusals name the slot and its holder, seat fixtures block walking and are entered through approach points.

tests.title: social verbs are registered in the one engine registry
catalog slots: campfire has 8 fire-circle places

converse: 4 people form a circle
converse refusals
campfire_circle with 10 people
gather onto a place region with an audience layout

seat fixtures and the campfire block walking
sitters walk around other chairs/benches
a seat whose approach point is walled in front and behind is refused

capabilities.approximate: Seats have no armrest or leg geometry: each fixture is one catalog box (a chair's includes its back), and the seated exemption is by activity, not per fixture. Approach points are not reserved (a person standing on one makes the sitter yield/replan). No turn-taking, gaze, gestures, group re-forming or automatic pre-emption; ambient never re-adopts a released person (SOCIAL.md).

capabilities.name: EUC / bicycle riding
capabilities.required: mount/ride_to/ride_loop/dismount on curvature- and acceleration-limited curves; stop short of and ask people to step aside; never use links; a parked vehicle is an obstacle; vehicle invariants catch close passes and teleports.

tests.title: EUC rides around the proving-ground wall
refused: a target on the deck (vehicles never use links)
person on the path: the EUC slows, stops
dismount: the rider steps off beside it
ride_loop: a closed 2-lap perimeter
bicycle in the 1.0 m passage is refused
kerbs: a 12 cm kerb a walker steps over blocks the EUC
vehicle invariants fire on deliberately invalid states

capabilities.approximate: No vehicle-vehicle collision or traffic rules (each sees the other's rider as a person). Vehicles are discs (the bicycle's 1.75 m length is not swept), with no lean, wheel or balance kinematics and no reversing; one level only (no links). Walkers see a rider as a 0.28 m person, not the vehicle disc. Proving ground only, not the campus (VEHICLES.md).

capabilities.name: Forklift to deck edges (rule-based)
capabilities.required: forklift_pick / forklift_deliver move a sheet from the ground onto a deck edge within lift range and fork reach, refusing unreachable placements and blocked lanes by name, stopping for people.

tests.title: forklift picks plywood off the ground and stages it on the 3 m deck
refused: a placement deeper than fork reach
refused: a 3.5 m surface is above the 3.2 m lift range
refused: an overhead beam lower than mast + load
refused: both fork-side approach lanes blocked
a person walking into the lane stops the truck
determinism: two identical runs of pick + deliver

capabilities.approximate: Rule-based, not dynamics: no tilt, pallets or dunnage, flat 1000 kg capacity (no load-moment chart), final alignment by standstill pivot + side-shift (no three-point turns); the truck body is not swept against people beyond the 1.5 m stop rule. Proving ground only (VEHICLES.md).

capabilities.name: Historical years as protected states (2020–2025)
capabilities.required: Each year 2020–2025 loads as a canonical, protected campus state with provenance on every obstacle; people route through that year's geometry; edits happen only in forks; a year room seeds it without touching 2026.

tests.title: each year 2020–2025 loads as a ground-only scene

building interiors are not walkable

extraction is deterministic: two --check runs
api: a historical year room (2022) seeds protected canonical mars-2022

capabilities.approximate: The years are the procedural reconstructions from app/history (hypothesis-grade geometry, not surveys), ground-only (decks block; no upper floors or stairs). Routes are proven in 2021 and 2022 only; no build or carry has been run in a historical year.

capabilities.name: Camera occlusion parity with the render
capabilities.required: The planner's readability (prisms + per-tick take-part occluders + person capsules) agrees with ray casts against the rendered mesh.

tests.title: part occluders: full boxes match entityCorners at any pose
a subject behind a rack-upright post is partly occluded
a person under a seated deck slab is occluded from a high wide
crew is see-through only within 0.6 m of its grip
a bystander between camera and subject occludes

capabilities.approximate: The parity numbers come from /studio against the rendered GLB (CAMERA_VERIFY.md, flagship take @ 2 Hz): meanPlanner 0.953 vs meanReal 0.963, maxAbsDiff 0.20, 1 sample differing by >= 0.2 (was 40), 0 hidden by the real mesh. That is one take, measured by the Playwright spec, which this report does not run; the engine tests here only pin the occluder geometry. Skinned bodies vs 0.2 m capsules still differ by up to 0.15.

capabilities.name: Incremental grids bit-identical
capabilities.required: Region-local grid updates on construction sync (and patched carry grids) equal a from-scratch buildGrids bit for bit: free cells, clearance and blocker names.

tests.title: updateGrids === buildGrids over 240 seeded random scenes
updateGrids: reordered or duplicate obstacles fall back
BlockerMap behaves as a Map<number, string>
build-bay on open ground (probe) + lab construction
campus flagship (staging-east crop)
Spatial.gridsFor === buildGrids for every carry plan

capabilities.approximate: Equality is checked on 240 random scenes and on every sync of the build-bay probe, the lab construction and the cropped campus flagship, not on the uncropped campus. Reordered or duplicate obstacle lists fall back to a full rebuild. Grids stay 0.1 m rasters with an exact EDT (no navmesh).

capabilities.name: Stable historical ids + migration
capabilities.required: Historical components keep `${assembly}-${kind}-${hash}` ids across unrelated scene edits; pinned names survive; legacy serial ids in saved layouts migrate through a frozen table.

tests.title: obstacle ids are the stable Kit ids (pinned names survive)

capabilities.approximate: The engine suite checks only that the extracted year obstacles carry the stable Kit ids and pinned names. The id scheme itself (determinism, insertion-independence) and the legacy-layout migration table are proven by deploy/history-ids.test.mjs (`npm test`), which this report does not run. Ids still change when a piece moves ~2.5 cm, rotates ~1° or changes kind/assembly.

capabilities.name: DO storage caps + isolation through the room
capabilities.required: EngineRoom (the Durable Object's code over SQLite) stores content-addressed state blobs, caps stored plans/takes per room without evicting referenced takes, and keeps replay, forks, plan staleness and year rooms isolated.

tests.title: api: EngineRoom stores states as content-addressed blobs
api: EngineRoom caps stored plans/takes per room
replay isolation (room)
fork isolation (room)
plan invalidation (room)
api: list (plans/takes/workspaces/cameras ledger) and delete_workspace

capabilities.approximate: Run over node:sqlite, not a real Durable Object; deploy/simulation-integration.mjs repeats isolation over MCP against `wrangler dev`/SIM_BASE and is not run here. Caps are counts per room-year (64 plans, 32 takes), not bytes: real DO storage size limits are not exercised.

capabilities.name: Deterministic trig across hosts
capabilities.required: Engine math uses pure IEEE-754 d* functions (never host Math.sin…), so Node, browsers and workerd produce the same state hashes.

tests.title: deterministic trig: <= 2 ulp of Math.*
deterministic trig: edge cases
datan2: quadrants, signed zeros
deterministic trig: golden bit patterns
engine source never calls the host transcendentals

capabilities.approximate: This suite runs on one host; golden bit patterns and the source scan are the in-suite guard. Cross-host equality is evidenced by the determinism probe hash (header above) matching the production browser stateHash (RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md, deploy 4) and Node = workerd take ids (HANDOFF.md), checked by hand, not by this report. Non-Chromium browsers are unverified.

capabilities.name: Mid-action resumability (walking/social subset)
capabilities.required: Runtime.snapshot/restore mid-action: a restored runtime steps tick-for-tick like an unpaused one; forks from a pause diverge deterministically; unsupported actions are refused by name.

tests.title: pause mid stair climb: restore continues identically
converse circle paused mid-formation resumes identically
gather paused mid-approach resumes identically
a sequence paused between steps
a snapshot during a carry is refused naming the action
an exec holding a closure is refused naming the path

capabilities.approximate: Walking, stairs and social verbs only: carry, construction lifts, vehicles and ambient_wander are not resumable (a snapshot is refused naming the action). Each restored runtime needs its own Spatial; the teleport check has no prior poses on the first restored tick (TAKES_AND_PLANS.md).

capabilities.name: Flagship on the full uncropped 2026 campus
capabilities.required: The campus flagship runs on the whole campus scene (7.6k obstacles, no crop) with 0 violations and the same final state as the ±40 m staging-east crop.

tests.title: ends physically identical to the cropped run
final-state hash === the cropped run (bit-identical)

capabilities.approximate: Completes with 0 violations; components end bit-identical and people within 1e-12 m, but the final-state hash differs and the build takes 36 ticks longer (the bit-identity test is a todo). Route vertices are cell centres computed from the grid origin (x0 + (i + 0.5)·cell), so the crop's origin (−12 vs −162) changes them by ulps; no route leaves the crop and the free cells match. About 2.5–3× the compute of the crop.
